# Tips

## Early game

- **Decide what to do with the survey party.** Destroy its radar and you get a command core, and Grubstake waits until
  {{< var arrival.survey_killed_delay_min >}} minutes after your first chemical science pack. Leave it and Grubstake
  lands {{< var arrival.survey_left_min >}} minutes after the party leaves, whether you are ready or not.
- **Put turrets on the ore you want next.** Grubstake's first camp lands on a rich field at least
  {{< var arrival.squat_tiles >}} tiles from your turrets and units. A few gun turrets on your next ore fields keep it
  off them.
- **Research Command bandwidth 1 before chemical science.** It needs only automation and logistic science packs, after
  Military 2 and Heavy armor, and it gives your first command core.
- **Automate heavy armor.** Every infantry order takes a suit of heavy armor. Make it, submachine guns and magazines on
  a line before you need troops in a hurry.
- **Build a relay with your first barracks.** With no working command relay you have no bandwidth, and the barracks
  holds its finished orders. Put a rally beacon down too, or new units stand where they were trained.
- **Put a threat scanner at each outpost.** Wired to a programmable speaker or a lamp, it tells you a raid has come
  before the turrets start firing.
- **Turn on Chat notices** in the map settings if you want to hear about raids and sieges as they start. Only first
  landings and destroyed bases are announced without it.

## Against Grubstake

- **Put a drill on every patch you plan to use.** A burner drill is enough. Grubstake prospects only ore that none of
  your drills works, so one cheap drill keeps the patch yours until you build there.
- **Run exposed belts underground.** A skim needs a belt tile to park beside. Undergrounds across the stretch your
  turrets do not cover leave it nothing to take.
- **Check your outposts before dark.** Its raids, skims and claim jumps leave only at night. Daylight is the time to
  move turrets and finish an outpost's defenses.
- **Keep spare machines in your logistic network.** Raiders leave ghosts where they took your machines, and your robots
  rebuild them at once from what is in storage.
- **Read your power statistics.** A consumer you never built whose draw climbs every few minutes is a power tap.
  Follow the amber pylons back to find it.
- **Pay the trade post in circuits or modules.** Plates are worth little to Grubstake. A few stacks of circuits buy a
  much longer truce than a chest full of iron.
- **Do not chase raiders into spawners.** The biters let Grubstake's units through and turn on yours.

## Against Kessler-Hayashi

- **Keep what matters deep behind your turrets.** A siege's mortars stand just outside your turrets' reach and outrange
  them only a little. Roboports, substations and assemblers well behind the turret line are out of their reach, and
  only a howitzer can touch them.
- **Hit the guns while they are assembled.** The escort holds just outside your turrets while the pods come down, and
  each gun is defenseless until the deploy ends. A gun destroyed then is lost to that siege.
- **Put an artillery turret behind each wall that faces its camp.** It kills a siege's howitzer by itself, and the
  artillery targeting remote lets it reach the mortars.
- **Give each field dome its own power.** A dome is up only while powered. On the same poles as your turrets, one cut
  takes down both.
- **Bring a border stake when you pay an invoice.** The truce is your only chance to set a border, and the border
  outlasts the truce.
- **Clear the spawners between your factory and its camp yourself.** Their attacks on Kessler-Hayashi are what it
  bills you for.
- **Guard your small outposts too.** Anything an operation destroys resets the count of failures that makes a camp
  stand down.
- **Cover the inside of your wall.** Its assault walks in through the breach and goes for your roboports, then your
  turrets. A second line of turrets behind the wall meets it there.
- **Give your laser line power to spare.** A lightning tank takes {{< var kh.tesla_drain_pct >}}% of a struck
  turret's charge. A grid with spare generation and accumulators by the turrets refills it almost at once.

## Against Synthexis

- **Get Bred-biter telemetry early.** Fighting Synthexis unlocks it (see [Spoils](spoils.qmd#field-studies)). Wire the
  *Synthexis's scout* signal to a speaker and to your rally beacons: a scout comes before every wave.
- **Attack-move into a culture.** A rally beacon's advance and the command tool's attack order go only for corporation
  targets. Send squads onto incubators and biochambers with attack-move, flamethrower troopers in front for the swarms.
- **Defend every side.** A wave takes the way in your turrets cover least, and a way that held costs more next time.
  A weak side is where the next wave comes.
- **Leave room behind the wall.** Bursters blow up at the wall and damage the turrets close to it. Turrets set a few
  tiles back take less.
- **Kill bursters before they arrive.** A burster that has stopped and started to swell always bursts. Turrets that
  reach well past the wall get them on the way, and a big burster killed short of its turret bursts with its core alone.
- **Spread your turrets out.** A big burster is sent at a turret and damages every turret around it, so a tight
  cluster loses several at once.
- **Build walls in depth.** Each wall behind the first costs a siege another rank of big bursters, and the rest of its
  wave waits until all of them are open.
- **Mix fire with lasers.** Where flamethrowers and mines do most of its killing, it spreads its big bursters over
  points no one flamethrower covers two of. Lasers along the whole face cover every point.
- **Bury the power and the ammo feed.** A wave past your wall heads for your power and the inserters that load your gun
  turrets. Keep both well inside, behind a second line of turrets.
- **Defoliate an incubator.** Kill the tumors near it, then throw a defoliant on it. Off the creep, it starves and goes
  back to the wild after {{< var synthexis.starve_min >}} minutes.
- **The field dome and the flak turret do nothing here.** No Synthexis breed fires shells or flies.
